# `libdrm_client.so`

The C library the FairPlay provider loads with `dlopen`. It starts Apple's
Android FairPlay libraries through libhybris, signs in, opens key contexts
and decrypts samples. `crates/fairplay-provider/src/ffi.rs` lists the
functions Slipmat calls.

`make fairplay-provider` copies this directory to a scratch directory, builds
the library there and copies only `libdrm_client.so` into the bundle under
`target/`. This directory is only read. Running `make` here directly builds in
place.

This copy is maintained by hand. Check upstream changes against the notes
below before taking them.

## Third-party sources

Recorded on 2026-11-22. Most of this directory was not written for Slipmat,
and not all of it was written for Adam.

### How `main.c` and `import.h` were identified as wrapper's

- `main.c` opens with a Chinese header describing itself as the Android-side
  program of the Apple Music FairPlay decryption wrapper, started by
  `wrapper.c` / `wrapper-rootless.c`.
- It lists wrapper's TCP services and ports: decrypt on 10020, M3U8 on 20020,
  account on 30020. Those are the defaults documented by the wrapper project.
- Its decrypt protocol, `[1B len][adam][1B len][uri]` then length-prefixed
  samples, is the one Adam's Go engine spoke.

Copies of wrapper are published at
[AMDL-Web/wrapper](https://github.com/AMDL-Web/wrapper) (formerly under
WorldObservationLog), [kjmesu/wrapper](https://github.com/kjmesu/wrapper) and
[codeberg.org/bl/wrapper-fork](https://codeberg.org/bl/wrapper-fork). Its
original author and licence were not established. Settle both before Slipmat
distributes this code or a library built from it: Slipmat is GPL-3.0-or-later.

### What the build leaves out

wrapper exists to decrypt and save tracks. `main.c` also contains a "key-port"
service (40020) that hands out content keys for offline decryption, captured
with Dobby code hooks. Slipmat's build keeps all of that out, which is what
hard rule 1 requires:

- The key-port service and its key export are inside `#ifndef DRM_LIB_BUILD`,
  and the Makefile always defines `DRM_LIB_BUILD`.
- `native/dobby.h` is a stub: every hook install reports failure.
- The built library imports no `socket`, `bind`, `listen` or `accept`, and
  contains no content-key, key-server or hook symbols, so it opens no network
  service. Re-check after any upstream change:

  ```sh
  nm -D --undefined-only libdrm_client.so | grep -wE 'socket|bind|listen|accept'
  nm libdrm_client.so | grep -iE 'content_key|key_server|r1_capture|Dobby'
  ```

  Both should print nothing.

The source for those parts is still in `native/main.c`, switched off.
